title: ChatAndBuild Launches Shared Memory Layer to Sync Context Across AI Models
summary:
The startup has introduced a persistent memory store that separates a user's project history from the specific large language model being used for reasoning. This layer, called Living Brain, allows users to maintain consistent context across various AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and Codex, eliminating the need to re-explain requirements when switching tools. The system integrates with connected AI agents through an API or the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

ChatAndBuild reports that by retrieving only relevant memories rather than the entire conversation history, Living Brain uses up to 22.6x fewer tokens per question and can reduce the cost per task by as much as 95%. Internal benchmarks for the tool include a 92.2% score on LoCoMo and a median retrieval time of 464ms, with a median end-to-end answer time of 3.7s.

We decoupled memory from the model.

Living Brain is one persistent brain for ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Codex and your own agents. Write in one, retrieve in any.

LLMs have parameters. Living Brain has plasticity.

selectedTweets.text:
Memory is becoming its own layer in the AI stack, separate from whichever model does the reasoning.

@livingbrain treats AI models as swappable engines and your accumulated context as the part that stays. Agents plug in through MCP or an API, so changing the model or agent framework leaves the memory intact.

Up to 95% lower cost per task. 3.7s median end-to-end answer.

Instead of sending the model your entire history every time, Living Brain picks only the few stored memories relevant to the current question and sends those, so the model processes far fewer tokens (up to 22.6x fewer), which is what cuts the cost per task by up to 95%.

ChatGPT and Claude each keep their own private memory of you, and neither can read the other’s. Living Brain moves that memory into a separate store that both tools, plus your own agents, can read and write.
